title: you look like you love me
awards: CMA Musical Event of the Year (2024)
ACM Music Event of the Year (2025)
ACM Visual Media of the Year (2025)
tldr: A spoken-word duet: lonely at a bar at 22, she spots a dancing cowboy, hands him a beer and tells him he looks like he loves her; Riley Green answers from his side. It hit #1 on Billboard Country Airplay and went 4x Platinum.
about:
What does 'you look like you love me' mean? It is, in Langley's words, 'a cute little love song'. In the first spoken verse she is 22, alone at a bar, until she sees a cowboy dancing, walks up, hands him a beer and confesses she has fallen for him. In the second verse Riley Green speaks from the cowboy's side and returns the feeling, and they sing the last chorus together.

Langley first wrote it with Aaron Raitiere; Green heard it on tour and wrote the second verse. Will Bundy produced it. It came out June 21, 2024 ahead of her debut album Hungover, went to country radio in August 2024, and became her first Billboard Hot 100 entry.

It reached #1 on Billboard Country Airplay (her first) and #30 on the Hot 100, and the RIAA has certified it 4x Platinum. It won Musical Event of the Year at the 2024 CMA Awards, Single of the Year at the 2025 ACM Awards, and Video of the Year at the 2025 CMA Awards.

title: weren't for the wind
tldr: A warning to future boyfriends: she is a rolling stone, as restless as the wind. Inspired by drives through Wyoming, it peaked at #18 on the Hot 100 and #2 on Billboard Country Airplay.
about:
What does 'weren't for the wind' mean? It is a mid-tempo warning to anyone who falls for her: she has rolling-stone tendencies, and she compares her free spirit to the changing wind. Langley has said it came from driving through Wyoming, with its open land and horses running alongside the road, and that the song 'just fell out'.

She wrote it with Johnny Clawson and Joybeth Taylor, and Will Bundy produced it. It first came out October 4, 2024 and appears on Still Hungover, the November 2024 deluxe edition of her debut album. It went to country radio January 2, 2025. The video (March 25, 2025), co-directed by Langley and Wales Toney, shows her breaking off an engagement to a fiance who tries to stifle her music dreams.

It became her highest-charting Hot 100 song at the time (#18) and reached #2 on Billboard Country Airplay and #4 on Hot Country Songs. The RIAA has certified it 3x Platinum.

title: nicotine
tldr: 'nicotine' compares a person to a habit you cannot quit. It came out in March 2024 as a promotional single ahead of her debut album Hungover.
about:
What does 'nicotine' mean? The song uses a cigarette habit as a metaphor for a relationship: something you know is bad for you and keep coming back to anyway.

Langley wrote it with Zachary Kale, Jon Nite and Joybeth Taylor, and Will Bundy produced it, as he did the rest of Hungover. It was released March 22, 2024 as a promotional single and became track 4 on Hungover (August 2, 2024).

title: paint the town blue
tldr: 'Paint the Town Blue' flips 'paint the town red': instead of a night out celebrating, she heads to the bar to drink away a breakup while pretending it doesn't hurt. It is a heartbreak song dressed up as a party song, written with Rhett Akins, Will Bundy and Travis Wood.
about:
What does 'Paint the Town Blue' mean? It turns the phrase 'paint the town red' upside down. Since the breakup she has been trying to paint things red, going out and acting like she is fine, but the chorus admits what is really happening: she is at the bar, she won't go home until she forgets, and the color of the night is blue.

It is a heartbreak song disguised as a honky-tonk banger: the drinking is there to drown the hurt, not celebrate.

Langley wrote it with Rhett Akins, Will Bundy and Travis Wood, and Bundy produced it. It came out October 13, 2023 as a promotional single ahead of her debut album Hungover (2024).

title: choosin' texas
producer: Ella Langley, Ben West & Miranda Lambert
tldr: 'Choosin' Texas' is about a woman realizing the man she loves is about to leave her for a Texas woman: she thought he was falling for her and Tennessee, but every sign (down to his love of 'Amarillo by Morning') says his heart always belonged to Texas. Written with Miranda Lambert, Luke Dick and Joybeth Taylor, it became her first Hot 100 #1.
about:
What does 'Choosin' Texas' mean? It is a heartbreak song told before the breakup is official. The narrator believed her man was falling in love with her and with Tennessee; the song is her slowly admitting he is going to choose Texas, and a Texas woman, instead. Texas works on two levels: the actual woman, and the life and home he never stopped missing.

The chorus is about signs she missed. It 'doesn't take a crystal ball' to see where his heart is: he loves 'Amarillo by Morning' (the Terry Stafford song George Strait made famous), and the lyric also nods to Jerry Reed's 'East Bound and Down' and Ronnie Milsap's 'Smoky Mountain Rain'.

The song came out of an October 2024 writing retreat with Miranda Lambert, Luke Dick and Joybeth Taylor. Lambert was telling stories about getting pulled over with Texas plates, Langley came up with the line 'She's from Texas, I can tell', and the song was finished in about 30 minutes. Lambert also sings background vocals, and Langley, Lambert and Ben West produced it.

Released October 17, 2025 as the lead single from Dandelion, it became her first Billboard Hot 100 #1 and spent 24 non-consecutive weeks on top, a record for the longest-running #1 in the chart's history. The video, released April 1, 2026, was filmed at the Stagecoach Ballroom in Fort Worth and stars Luke Grimes.

title: don't mind if i do
album: Don't Mind If I Do (Riley Green)
tldr: Riley Green's song featuring Ella Langley: a man drinking to forget an ex who secretly wants her back, and her answer that she doesn't mind if he does. It hit #1 on Billboard Country Airplay.
about:
What does 'Don't Mind If I Do' mean? Riley Green sings as a man drinking whiskey to get over an ex while hoping to rekindle things. Langley sings backing vocals in the second verse, hinting she misses him too, then takes the lead in the final chorus from the ex's point of view: she wants him to say how he really feels, and she doesn't mind if he does.

It is Riley Green's song (he wrote it) from his 2024 album Don't Mind If I Do, produced by Dann Huff. It was first released September 6, 2024 and went to country radio July 21, 2025. It is the pair's second duet after 'you look like you love me'.

It reached #1 on Billboard Country Airplay, #5 on Hot Country Songs and #23 on the Hot 100, and the RIAA has certified it Platinum.

title: never met anyone like you
tldr: It sounds like a love song until the bridge, when the guitars turn heavy and she reveals he cheated on her with her friend. 'Never met anyone like you' turns out to be an insult. Written with HARDY, who features.
about:
What does 'Never Met Anyone Like You' mean? It is a bait-and-switch. For most of the song Langley praises her man over acoustic guitar: his charisma, his music taste, how he treats his mother, 'one in a million'. In the bridge the instrumental turns hard-rock and she reveals he cheated on her with her friend and blamed her for it. The title phrase flips from compliment to insult.

The idea was HARDY's: he proposed a song called 'Never Met Anyone Like You' that would sound like love but reveal the opposite. Langley wrote it with Michael Hardy (HARDY) and Jordan Schmidt, Schmidt produced it, and HARDY is featured.

It was released June 27, 2025 as a standalone single, before Dandelion. It peaked at #39 on Billboard Hot Country Songs.

title: be her
producer: Ella Langley, Ben West & Miranda Lambert
tldr: 'Be Her' is Ella Langley describing the woman she wants to become: grounded in her faith, comfortable in her own skin, living a simpler, more honest life. It is a self-worth song about the gap between who she is and who she is trying to be. She wrote it with Jordan Schmidt, HARDY and Smith Ahnquist.
about:
What does 'Be Her' mean? It is an introspective song about self-worth. The lyric sketches an idealized version of a woman who is grounded in her faith and completely comfortable in her own skin, and the narrator wants to be her: simpler, more authentic, less at war with herself.

Langley wrote it with Jordan Schmidt, Michael Hardy (HARDY) and Smith Ahnquist; HARDY has said the song 'basically wrote itself' in about 30 minutes. It is a steel-soaked, '90s-leaning neo-traditional ballad, produced by Langley with Ben West and Miranda Lambert.

The music video (February 13, 2026), co-directed by Langley and Wales Toney, plays out the same idea: the gap between who she is and who she wants to become. 'Be Her' went to country radio March 23, 2026 as the second Dandelion single and peaked at #2 on the Hot 100, held off the top only by her own 'Choosin' Texas'.

title: loving life again
producer: Ella Langley, Ben West & Miranda Lambert
tldr: 'Loving Life Again' is about coming back from depression. Langley has said it was inspired by her mental-health struggles in 2025, when she canceled shows and went home to her parents; the title is what she told ERNEST when he asked how she was doing after she came back.
about:
What does 'Loving Life Again' mean? It is a recovery song. Langley explained on stage in Chattanooga that it came from the mental-health struggles that followed her early success, including the stretch in 2025 when she canceled shows and went home to her parents to recover.

ERNEST, whom she had confided in, asked how she was doing once she was back. Her answer, 'Well, looks like I'm back to loving life again', became the hook. They wrote the chorus together and finished the song a few days later with Devin Dawson. ERNEST also sings background vocals.

The first verse compares hard times to changing seasons and admits how easy it is to get stuck in a dark state of mind; by the chorus she has found peace in music and joy in her life again, with childhood memories (riding her quarter horse through the pines, her grandmother calling her inside) as the anchor. She debuted it live at the Ryman with ERNEST in November 2025, and it went to country radio July 13, 2026 as the fourth Dandelion single.

title: dandelion
producer: Ella Langley, Austin Goodloe, Ben West & Miranda Lambert
tldr: 'Dandelion' is Ella Langley comparing herself to the flower: often dismissed as a weed and overlooked, but able to survive harsh conditions. It is about her free spirit, resilience and country roots, and a warning to a would-be lover that she does things her own way. It is the title track of her 2026 album.
about:
What does 'Dandelion' mean? Langley compares herself to the dandelion: a plant people dismiss as a weed, but one that thrives in harsh conditions. The song uses it to describe her free spirit, wild side and resilience, her feeling of being overlooked earlier in her career, and her lasting connection to her country roots. She also applies the same independence to love, warning a potential partner about her unconventional ways.

In the album trailer she said dandelions are 'masters of survival' that carry 'hope, healing, and resilience', and that the record 'has so much growth in it'. She also liked that dandelion tea is known as a liver detox, a fitting follow-up to her debut album Hungover.

Langley wrote it with Joybeth Taylor, Austin Goodloe and Brett Tyler and produced it with Austin Goodloe, Ben West and Miranda Lambert. Released January 30, 2026 as a promotional single, it debuted at #7 on Billboard Hot Country Songs and became the title track of Dandelion (April 10, 2026).

title: i can't love you anymore
producer: Ella Langley, Austin Goodloe & Ben West
tldr: A duet with Morgan Wallen about a dysfunctional relationship two people are too worn out to keep and too attached to leave. Released April 24, 2026 on the Dandelion reissue; it reached #1 on Billboard Country Airplay.
about:
What does 'I Can't Love You Anymore' mean? It is a mid-tempo heartbreaker about a dysfunctional relationship, caught between exhaustion and the inability to separate. The title is the line both of them keep saying without being able to make it true.

Langley wrote it with Austin Goodloe and Joybeth Taylor and sent it to Morgan Wallen; she produced it with Goodloe and Ben West. Reviewers compared its '70s-leaning sound to Fleetwood Mac.

The pair announced it on stage in Tuscaloosa on April 18, 2026, the eighth time she had joined Wallen on his tour, and performed it live for the first time that night. It was released April 24, 2026 on the reissue of Dandelion. It reached #1 on Billboard Country Airplay, #3 on Hot Country Songs and #4 on the Hot 100.

title: here for the party
album: Here for the Party (Gretchen Wilson re-recording)
tldr: Gretchen Wilson's 2004 party anthem, re-recorded in 2026 with Ella Langley featured. Released June 26, 2026.
about:
What does 'Here for the Party' mean? It is Gretchen Wilson's 2004 rowdy-girl anthem: a woman announcing she came to have a good time, not to be told how to behave.

This version is Wilson's 2026 re-recording of her own song, featuring Ella Langley, released June 26, 2026 as the first taste of a fully re-recorded edition of Wilson's debut album. The two first sang it together at Langley's Ryman Auditorium show in November 2025, and opened the 2026 CMA Fest broadcast with it.

The songwriters are the original ones, Gretchen Wilson, John Rich and Big Kenny, because it is their song; Ella and Gretchen are the voices on this version.

title: butterfly season
producer: Ella Langley, Ben West & Miranda Lambert
tldr: 'Butterfly Season' uses a butterfly's metamorphosis as a metaphor for personal growth: choosing to leave an older version of yourself behind, even when you can't see how it turns out. It is a hopeful duet with Miranda Lambert from Dandelion, written by Langley, Lambert, Luke Dick and Joybeth Taylor.
about:
What does 'Butterfly Season' mean? It is a song about transformation. The butterfly's metamorphosis stands in for deliberately leaving an old version of yourself behind and growing into a new one, with spring, and planting flowers, as images of change.

It lands on Dandelion after a hard stretch for Langley, who stepped away from touring in 2025 to focus on her mental health, which is why critics read it as a hopeful song about reinvention rather than a sad one. Miranda Lambert duets on it.

Langley wrote it with Lambert, Luke Dick and Joybeth Taylor (the same four who wrote 'Choosin' Texas'), and it was produced by Langley, Lambert and Ben West. It is track 16 on Dandelion (April 10, 2026).

title: jaded
tldr: 'Jaded' is a call-and-response duet in which Koe Wetzel and Ella Langley play two people who have been hurt so many times they have put up emotional armor. They trade questions about who broke their hearts and land in the same place: after enough heartbreak, nothing shocks you anymore.
about:
What does 'Jaded' mean? It is a duet about what heartbreak leaves behind. Koe Wetzel and Ella Langley trade lines as two guarded people asking each other who hurt them and why they got so hard to reach, and both arrive at the same answer. There is no sign it is about a specific ex; it is a story song.

Langley and ERNEST had sketched the idea about a year earlier ('How'd you get so jaded?'), and it was finished when Wetzel joined them and Jordan Schmidt for a Nashville write on January 14, 2026. Schmidt and Gabe Simon produced it.

It is Wetzel's song, with Langley featured, and appears on the deluxe edition of his album The Night Champion. It is their second duet after 'That's Why We Fight' from Langley's 2023 EP Excuse the Mess.

title: bottom of your boots
producer: Ella Langley, Ben West & Miranda Lambert
tldr: 'Bottom of Your Boots' asks a partner to prove it: if he really loves her, she wants all of it, from the bottom of his boots to the top of his hat. The title came from a pep talk from her father.
about:
What does 'Bottom of Your Boots' mean? It is a song about wanting full commitment. Langley asks her partner to say how he really feels and to show it completely if he truly loves her.

She has said the title came from her father, who told her during a hard week, 'I love you from the bottom of my boots to the top of my hat.' She wrote it with Will Bundy and Jon Nite and produced it with Ben West and Miranda Lambert, and debuted it live at a Nashville pop-up show in early April 2026.

It is an album track from Dandelion (April 10, 2026), and the album's strongest-charting deep cut: #20 on the Billboard Hot 100 and #4 on Hot Country Songs.

title: hell at night
producer: Charlie Handsome, UV Killin Em & Bandplay
tldr: A country-rap breakup song: BigXthaPlug and Ella Langley both wish a little hell on the exes who did them wrong, hoping guilt keeps them up at night. It reached #26 on the Hot 100.
about:
What does 'Hell at Night' mean? Both singers are in the aftermath of a breakup and hoping their exes suffer for how they treated them. Langley sings that she should be moving on peacefully but can't get past the anger; BigXthaPlug lists the misfortunes he hopes land on his ex. The shared wish is that guilt keeps them from sleeping at night.

It is BigXthaPlug's song featuring Langley, released August 8, 2025 as the third single from his album I Hope You're Happy, and produced by Charlie Handsome, UV Killin Em and Bandplay. Both artists teased it on TikTok before release.

It peaked at #26 on the Billboard Hot 100 and #8 on Hot Country Songs, and the RIAA has certified it Platinum.
